evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 跑 entry
evidence.field: 形義通解; graphic analysis; semantic attestations
evidence.text: The database analyzes 跑 as 从足，包声 and gives the original sense as an animal pawing the ground with its feet. It quotes Guangyun’s gloss 足跑地也, a horse pawing the ground in 西京雜記, and a Tang poem about a hungry horse pawing snow. It also cites a Tang poem for running, then later examples for fleeing, losing, and going about business. These examples document uses across periods; the source does not establish every semantic bridge or an exact first-use date.
evidence.kind: character-specific dictionary entry and cited attestations
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, 跑 entry
evidence.field: 研訂瀏覽; forms and textual history
evidence.text: The entry says 跑 is absent from Shuowen and appears in 龍龕手鑑, glossed 音雹，秦言蹴也. It summarizes Guangyun’s two readings and senses: level-tone 肴 rhyme 足跑地也 (薄交切), and entering-tone 覺 rhyme 秦人言蹴 (蒲角切). It also discusses a variant whose 包-like component was altered toward 色, suggesting either graphic confusion or copying alteration; this is an explicit proposed corruption account for that related variant, not evidence that the standard graph 跑 itself arose by corruption.
evidence.kind: official dictionary editorial discussion citing historical dictionaries
evidence.title: [A04008] 跑 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, 跑 entry

evidence.text: The page lists Mandarin readings páo, bó, pǎo and Cantonese readings paau2, paau4, and lists 趵 as a graph variant. This page does not establish a corruption relationship between 趵 and 跑 or the ancient graphic development of 跑.

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 小學堂字形演變 database, overview
evidence.text: The database describes itself as a collection of representative forms from oracle-bone, bronze, Chu bamboo and silk, small-seal, and other databases, with source and form-analysis information. Its current overview reports 13,779 head entries and 44,282 forms. This overview establishes the resource’s scope but is not a record of a 跑 glyph; no usable character-specific 跑 image record was retrieved.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形演變

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 小學堂, rights notice
evidence.text: The official notice states that glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the database query interface are offered under CC0 1.0. This permission is scoped to those query-interface glyph assets and attributes; it does not provide a selected 跑 image because no specific image record was retrieved.
evidence.title: 小學堂版權聲明

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction table, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)
evidence.text: The table gives 包 Mandarin bāo, Middle Chinese paew, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *pˤ<r>u, gloss ‘wrap, bundle’. The local baxtersagart.tsv row supplied for this research matches this transcription. No 跑 entry was supplied in the local table, so a same-system B–S comparison for host and sound component is unavailable here. The CUHK database independently identifies 包 as the sound component; the reconstruction alone does not establish that role.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.text: The official U+8DD1 Unihan record was directly attempted but unavailable through the web tool during this research. A local row was supplied as 跑 → pǎo, but that repository row is not used as external evidence or as evidence for an ancient sound relationship.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, 跑 entry
evidence.text: The entry explicitly says 跑 is absent from Shuowen and first appears in 龍龕手鑑, where it is glossed ‘秦言蹴也’. It reports a related variant with 包 altered toward 色 and considers mistaken similarity or copying alteration as possible explanations. This supports a cautious account of a later anomalous variant, but does not establish any pre-Liao paleographic form or an earlier graph for the standard character.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the official Taiwan Ministry of Education character-variant entries. They state that 跑 is absent from Shuowen, give the Longkan attestation and Guangyun distinctions, and discuss a possible graphic alteration in a related variant. A linked Longkan image request failed with cache miss.

Opened the official Xiaoxuetang rights notice and guide. The rights notice limits CC0 to glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through its query interface; no selected 跑 asset was obtained.

gaps: No specific Xiaoxuetang query result, exact 跑 form label, or direct rendered glyph URL was retrieved, and no inspected Commons file was an actual 跑 glyph. Therefore no historical_glyph candidate is proposed. The sources inspected document a Later Tang/Liao-era dictionary attestation and some later forms but not an early paleographic sequence.

The MOE dictionary’s researched summary says 跑 is absent from Shuowen and first recorded in 龍龕手鑑, with a gloss equivalent to ‘in Qin usage, kick’. Guangyun, compiled 1008, distinguishes pawing the ground from a Qin term for kicking. The precise chronology of the cited 西京雜記 passage and the actual manuscript witness for the quoted graph are not established here.

The CUHK database presents the semantic development from pawing to running and later fleeing/business uses, supported by examples. These attestations do not demonstrate every semantic bridge, nor do they independently prove the full chronology of extensions.

The MOE note proposes graphic error or copying alteration for a variant that changes 包 toward 色. That does not show that the standard form 跑 itself was corrupted. No source inspected supports a claim that the graph arose from an earlier unrelated character.

CUHK and MOE identify 包 as the phonetic component; both modern pronunciations are supplied only by local rows here. Official Unicode U+8DD1 and U+5305 pages failed to open, so external official Unihan click-through evidence for current kMandarin cannot be supplied in this run. Baxter–Sagart’s published table gives 包 *pˤ<r>u, but the local table has no 跑 row; CUHK records two medieval fanqie readings for 跑. No same-system host/component Baxter–Sagart comparison is established.
The online sources inspected did not establish a secure external Baxter–Sagart reading for 跑. Zhengzhang readings in the dossier are secondary listings and are not conflated with Baxter–Sagart.

No source reuse recommendation is made: the sources are paraphrased and cited by character-specific page; permission for a repeatable bulk extract was not established. Xiaoxuetang’s CC0 notice covers specific query-interface glyph assets and attributes only.

limitations.text: Searches and inspection did not establish any actual 跑 glyph image candidate with a verified identity, direct image URL, and reuse provenance. Xiaoxuetang’s form-history pages and rights notice were checked, but no character-specific form record/image was retrieved; Commons results were not 跑 glyphs. Taiwan MOE lists a Longkan form-image witness, but its linked image request failed. No glyph is selected.
